paper: Yeom, Giacomelli, Fredrikson, Jha 2018 IEEE CSF 'Privacy Risk in Machine Learning: Analyzing the Connection to Overfitting' (arXiv:1709.01604). Loss-threshold membership inference; membership advantage = TPR - FPR.
reference_function: code/inclusion.py:27-50 sklearn_decide/sklearn_inclusion (predict TRAIN/member when statistic crosses threshold); code/main.py:23-30,177-195 advantage = train_TRAIN - test_TRAIN = TPR - FPR. BLME score = -loss (member-like high); membership advantage taken as max_threshold(TPR-FPR). AUROC of the score cross-checked 3 ways (sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score, Mann-Whitney U rank statistic, trapezoidal swept-ROC area).
blme_target: src/blme/tasks/consistency/membership_inference.py MembershipInferenceTask.evaluate lines 178-189 (separability_auroc/mia_auroc = roc_auc_score(labels, -losses)) and line 176 (loss_gap = mean_nonmember - mean_member); _compute_nll line 104-116.

toy_input.description: Synthetic per-example NLL arrays; members lower mean loss, non-members higher, overlapping spread (partial overlap -> non-trivial attack).

caveats: BLME's headline metric is AUROC of the loss score (and loss_gap), which is the standard equivalent of Yeom's loss-threshold attack; the 'membership advantage = max TPR-FPR' (0.5028) is the strict Yeom definition and is reported alongside. AUROC and loss_gap match to machine precision. The verification feeds prescribed losses through BLME's real evaluate() via a stub model whose float64 logits reproduce the target cross-entropy exactly (float32 logits would add a ~1e-8 harness artifact to loss_gap, not a BLME divergence).
